evidence.paraphrase: The narrator explains the technical practice by which a switchboard operator can eavesdrop on any call.
evidence.quote: "Listening in" is a plug-shifting process whereby the telephone-operator may hear any conversation over the wire. In some States, I understand, it is a misdemeanor.

evidence.paraphrase: The narrator explains how leaving a switch open lets another caller tap into an ongoing call.
evidence.quote: And it means the switch has carelessly been left open, so that anybody calling up can tap the wire.

evidence.paraphrase: A description of a social/economic development in which luxury apartment-houses proliferated amid high living costs.
evidence.quote: When the high cost of living first menaced our suffering land, scores of such apartment-houses sprang into life, in order that New Yorkers might do their bit toward the upkeep of high prices.

evidence.paraphrase: Daisy has a strong emotional collapse upon realizing the truth about the couple.
evidence.quote: Daisy Reynolds slumped forward upon the switchboard desk, her face in her hands, her slim body a-shake. She felt as though her every nerve had been wrenched.

evidence.paraphrase: The reality of Madeline sharply contrasts with the idealized image Daisy had imagined.
evidence.quote: This woman framed in the doorway was Madeline--_her_ Madeline? This woman whose dumpy figure was swathed in a bedraggled negligee that had once been clean!

evidence.paraphrase: Daisy is pained as her idealized image of Karl is shattered by his actual appearance.
evidence.quote: Daisy by this time should have been past surprise. Yet her preconceived vision of Karl--of young, athletic, hero-featured Karl--died hard and in much and sudden pain.

evidence.paraphrase: The narrator compares Daisy's imaginative construction of Karl to scientific reconstruction from a fossil.
evidence.quote: As scientists reconstruct an entire fossil animal from a single bone of its left hind leg, so Daisy Reynolds built up a vision of Karl from his deep and powerful voice.
